content.comment_body: Hello, I have some questions regarding [product_name] PLCs. I am working with two units, which I will refer to as PLC_1 and PLC_2, along with an HMI panel. I've noticed two possible ways to connect these devices: using a Master-Slave setup or via virtual memory (VM) available in [version_no]. My first question is about the difference between these two methods. I attempted to access I1 from PLC_2 in the PLC_1 program, but this only works with the Master-Slave option; I set up PLC_1 as master and PLC_2 as slave. My second question concerns visualizing data in the HMI panel. When using Master/Slave communication, I have trouble addressing tags in [product_name] engineering software. For example, how should I address a slave I/O like NI1? I tried setting up two connections in the software—one for master and one for slave. Signals from the master work as expected, but I have issues with the slave connection; when I create a tag (e.g., button_1 using the slave connection and address I1), the events do not trigger. One solution I found was to use a marker (M1) in the master PLC program. Here's how I solved the issue: 1. Create two connections in [product_name] HMI software: one for the master, one for the slave. 2. In the PLC program, take NI1 and add a marker (M1) after this element. 3. In the HMI software, create a tag tied to connection_1 (master) and use address M0.0, which surprised me as I expected to use M1.0. If you have alternative solutions, please share. Thanks in advance. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi, 1. An HMI cannot read or write data directly to a slave device; the slave only communicates with its designated [product_name] master. 2. Regarding addressing in [product_name] systems: in these platforms, digital values are counted in binary format. For example, I1 in [product_name] corresponds to I0.0 in [product_name] conventions. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is working to establish communication between two [product_name] PLC units and an HMI panel, comparing Master-Slave and virtual memory methods. There are difficulties with tag addressing across systems, particularly in mapping PLC addresses to the HMI, which causes confusion when trying to visualize slave input signals.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a simple and transparent method for tag addressing between [product_name] PLCs and related software, enabling reliable visualization of inputs from both master and slave devices on their HMI panel.
